title: The Chryseum — Interior
purpose: What the party sees when they step inside. This is Roderic's faith made physical — the most impressive expression of the Luciferian religion he has ever walked into outside of Beaconhold's grand cathedral where he was raised. It is also Severin's domain, and his personality is imprinted on the space: immaculate, severe, certain. For Edric, this is hostile territory — a place run by a man who has turned his congregation against bards and storytellers. The floor should hint at what lies beneath: the pre-Luciferian shrine the party is actually here to find.
subject: The interior nave of the Chryseum, Aurelion's cathedral of the Light. A soaring sacred space where whiteglass, gold, and candlelight combine to create the sensation of standing inside captured light. The architecture is designed to overwhelm — to make the individual feel small and the institution feel absolute. Every surface communicates order, permanence, and doctrinal certainty. It is genuinely beautiful, and that beauty has teeth.

core_aesthetic.historical_context: Aurelion was once a crown jewel of the Imperium Lucis Aeternae — a vast Roman-analogous empire of light. The city sat atop rich gold deposits and the Imperium had the magical technology to extract it. The name itself echoes 'aurum.' Gold language runs through every institution: the Aureate (soldiers), the Assayer Sovereign, the Orate. But the Imperium fell centuries ago, the extraction technology was lost, and the gold is locked in inaccessible substrate beneath the city. Aurelion went from imperial capital to independent Middle Kingdom to conquered vassal of Beaconhold. It is now a county seat ruled by a count who answers to a distant king.
core_aesthetic.visual_philosophy: Gold that has tarnished. Grandeur that has been patched. Imperial architecture repurposed for smaller ambitions. Think Prague or Budapest — cities where you can see the layers of history and the gap between what the place once was and what it is now. Gilded domes gone green with verdigris. Broad imperial avenues lined with cramped market stalls. Monumental stonework being used as the foundation for timber tenements. A post-imperial Eastern European melancholy layered over Roman-scale bones.
core_aesthetic.the_interior_exception: Like the exterior, the Chryseum's interior is the one space in Aurelion where the golden aesthetic is fully maintained. The Church invests here. Gold leaf is fresh, stonework is clean, every surface is tended. But where the exterior shows this through contrast with the declining city outside, the interior shows it through intensity — the concentration of wealth and care in this single space feels almost aggressive. The Church is making a statement about where permanence lives.

setting: The central nave of the Chryseum, viewed from just inside the main entrance looking toward the altar at the far end. The full length and height of the space is visible. The viewer has just stepped through the doors and is taking it all in for the first time.

architecture.the_nave: A long, high central space with a vaulted ceiling rising to the interior of the golden dome. The proportions are deliberately overwhelming — built to make humans feel the scale of the divine. Colonnades or pillared arcades line both sides, creating side aisles that recede into shadow. The central axis draws the eye irresistibly from entrance to altar.
architecture.the_dome_interior: The underside of the golden dome is the visual climax of the space. Gold leaf, mosaic, or painted imagery depicting Lucifer's light radiating outward in geometric patterns — not figurative religious scenes but abstract radiance, rays, and concentric forms. The dome captures and concentrates the light entering from whiteglass panels around its base, creating a warm glow that fills the upper space like a second sun.
architecture.whiteglass_elements: Whiteglass panels set into the upper walls and around the dome's base serve as the primary light source. They do not function like stained glass — they are translucent, luminous, and generate their own cool blue-white light rather than filtering external sunlight. The effect is unique: a combination of the dome's warm gold radiance above and the whiteglass's cool eternal luminescence from the sides, creating a complex layered light environment that feels unlike natural illumination. The light in this space is engineered.
architecture.the_altar: A focal point at the far end of the nave — a raised platform with a large whiteglass piece as its centerpiece. This piece radiates the strongest, cleanest light in the building — cool, steady, unwavering. It is the visual and spiritual anchor of the entire space. Surrounding the altar: liturgical gold fixtures, candelabras, and prayer positions for clergy.
architecture.side_aisles: Darker than the central nave, receding into relative shadow. Smaller chapels or alcoves along the walls, each with its own smaller whiteglass element and candles. These are intimate spaces nested within the overwhelming whole — places where individual prayer happens under the institution's vast ceiling.
architecture.the_floor: Stone flooring laid in geometric patterns. Most of the pattern is consistent with Luciferian design — radial symmetry, light-motif geometry, precise and orderly. But in certain areas, particularly near the altar and along the central axis, the stone patterns shift subtly. Older geometric forms are visible — spiral motifs, growth-ring patterns, organic curves that do not match the Luciferian vocabulary. These are remnants of the pre-Luciferian structure the cathedral was built over. They have been incorporated into the floor rather than removed, perhaps because the builders could not remove them, or perhaps because they did not understand what they were. To an untrained eye they read as decorative variation. To someone looking for the shrine of Renewal beneath, they are a map.

atmosphere.light: The defining feature of the interior. Two distinct light sources layered together: the warm golden radiance reflected and concentrated by the dome above, and the cool blue-white luminescence of the whiteglass panels from the sides and altar. Together they create an otherworldly illumination — not candlelight, not sunlight, but something unique to this space. Incense haze hangs in the upper vaults, caught in the light, giving the air visible texture. Shafts and gradients of light move through the space with almost physical presence.
atmosphere.sound_implied: Though this is an image, the composition should suggest acoustic grandeur — the kind of space where a whisper carries and a sermon fills every corner. The vaulted ceiling and stone surfaces imply resonance. Severin's voice was trained to fill this space without shouting.
atmosphere.incense: Visible as haze in the upper portions of the nave, catching the light from the dome and whiteglass. It softens the edges of the architecture and adds depth to the light. Frankincense and something sharper — juniper — though of course only the visual effect of the smoke is relevant here.
atmosphere.temperature_implied: The space should feel cool. Stone, whiteglass, gold — nothing warm or soft. The light is impressive but not comforting. This is a place designed for awe, not intimacy.

figures.worshippers: A scattering of figures in the pews or prayer positions — not a full congregation, just the devoted attending outside of formal services. Heads bowed, postures still. Small against the architecture.
figures.clergy: One or two robed figures near the altar or in the side aisles, going about liturgical duties. Not Severin himself — he is reserved for his own portrait image — but his presence is felt through the space's severe perfection.
figures.scale: All figures are small. The architecture dominates absolutely. A human being in this space is meant to feel the disproportion between themselves and the institution.

lighting: The most complex lighting of any image in the set. Two primary sources: warm gold from the dome above (reflected, concentrated, radiant) and cool blue-white from the whiteglass panels and altar (self-generated, steady, eternal). These two light temperatures mix in the nave's middle space, creating gradients and layered illumination. Candlelight provides a third, smaller warm source at human scale — candelabras along the aisles and at the altar. Incense haze in the upper vaults diffuses and softens the dome light. The side aisles fall into relative shadow, with small pools of light from individual whiteglass elements and candles.
color_palette: warm radiant gold (dome interior, gold leaf, reflected light)
cool blue-white luminescence (whiteglass panels and altar piece)
candle-flame amber and warm yellow (candelabras, human-scale light)
pale sandstone and honey limestone (columns, walls, vaults)
deep shadow and charcoal (side aisles, recesses, the spaces between light sources)
incense gray-blue haze (upper vaults, softening edges)
liturgical gold accents (fixtures, trim, altar furniture)
subtle earth tones in the floor (the older geometric patterns standing out faintly against the Luciferian stonework)
mood: Sacred intimidation. The beauty is real — genuinely awe-inspiring, the kind of space that makes you hold your breath when you enter. But the awe is engineered. Every proportion, every light source, every surface is calibrated to produce a specific emotional response: you are small, the Light is vast, and Severin is its voice in this place. For Roderic, this should stir something deep — his faith's highest architectural expression. For Edric, this should feel like walking into the headquarters of the man who wants to silence him. The space does not care which reaction you have. It is certain of itself either way.
composition: Central perspective from the entrance looking down the nave toward the altar, with the dome overhead. Strong single-point perspective created by the colonnades and floor patterns converging on the altar and its whiteglass centerpiece. The dome fills the upper portion of the image. The floor patterns draw the eye forward along the central axis. The composition itself is an expression of the Luciferian design philosophy — ordered, symmetrical, directing attention toward the source of light.
details: The dome interior's gold surface showing geometric radiance patterns — rays, concentric circles, abstract light-motifs rather than figurative religious scenes
Whiteglass panels glowing with their own inner light, appearing ageless against the warm-toned stone around them
The altar's central whiteglass piece radiating the brightest, coolest light in the space — the spiritual focal point
Incense haze visible in the upper vaults, caught in crossing beams of gold and blue-white light
Floor patterns that shift subtly near the altar — older spiral and organic-curve motifs embedded among the Luciferian geometry, easy to miss but present
Candle flames providing warm intimate light at human scale, contrasting with the vast institutional light above
A single worshipper's upturned face caught in the mixed light — gold and blue-white together on human skin

The perfect cleanliness and maintenance of every surface — not a single stone out of place, not a single cobweb, not a single unpolished fixture. Severin's hand is visible in the space's immaculate severity.
style: Painterly fantasy illustration with the grandeur and atmospheric density of cathedral interior photography. Concept art quality. The tone of standing inside a space that was built to be the argument for its own faith — where architecture *is* theology. Strong use of layered light sources to create visual complexity and emotional texture. The image should make the viewer understand why Roderic believes and why Edric is afraid. Grounded and realistic, but heightened — this is the most visually impressive interior in the campaign so far.
aspect_ratio: 2:3 portrait — vertical composition to capture the full soaring height from floor to dome, emphasizing the overwhelming scale
do_not_include: Christian-specific iconography — no crosses, no saints, no biblical scenes. This is Luciferian: light, radiance, geometric precision, warding symbols
Stained glass in traditional colored-glass style — whiteglass is translucent and self-luminous, not colored filters for external light
Warmth or coziness — this space is impressive, not comfortable
Clutter, mess, or signs of neglect — the immaculate maintenance is a character trait of the space
Severin himself — he gets his own portrait image; his presence here is felt through the space, not shown
Visible magical effects like floating runes or glowing symbols — the whiteglass luminescence is the only supernatural visual element
Dark or horror elements — this is not an evil church, it is an authoritarian one. The threat is certainty, not corruption
Figurative religious art — Luciferian sacred imagery is abstract: light, geometry, radiance patterns
